content.title: How to Watch and Stream the 2026 March Madness Final Four and Championship Games
content.text: Azzi Fudd #35 of the UConn Huskies dribbles on February 18, 2026 in Villanova, Pennsylvania; Braylon Mullins #24 of the UConn Huskies on March 27, 2026 in Washington, DC. Credit : Bill Streicher/Getty; Emilee Chinn/Getty NEED TO KNOW There are four teams left in both the men's and women's March Madness tournamentAfter the Final Four games are played, the remaining two teams will compete in the 2026 National ChampionshipThe men's games will air on TBS and TNT, while the women's will be broadcast on ESPN and ABC March Madness is finally coming to an end! The annual NCAA Division I Women's and Men's Basketball National Championship tournament had no shortage of upsets, buzzer-beaters and dramatic moments over the last few weeks. The college basketball tournament will determine its men's and women's champions after they each play in the Final Four. In the men's tournament, the University of Illinois will face off against the University of Connecticut — who took home the title back-to-back in 2023 and 2024 — in the Final Four. On the other side of the bracket, the University of Arizona will compete against the University of Michigan. Meanwhile, the women's Final Four tournament has all the No. 1 seeds remaining — the University of South Carolina vs. the University of Connecticut and the University of Texas at Austin vs. the University of California, Los Angeles. The final two men's teams will compete in the National Championship on Monday, April 6, while the women's National Championship takes place the day before. Although the past men's games rotated on TNT, TBS and CBS, the remaining Final Four and Championship games will only be available to watch on TBS, TNT or TruTV. However, the women's games will air on ESPN and ABC. Here's everything to know about how to watch the March Madness Final Four and Championship games. Who's in the men's Final Four? Keaton Wagler #23 of the Illinois Fighting on March 28, 2026 in Houston, Texas; Braylon Mullins #24 of the UConn Huskies on March 29, 2026 in Washington, DC. Alex Slitz/Getty; Brett Wilhelm/NCAA Photos via Getty UConn (No. 2) upset several brackets in the Elite Eight when they beat Duke (No. 1) in a buzzer-beater moment and made it to the Final Four semifinals. The Huskies will take on the Illinois Illini (No. 3), who sent the Iowa Hawkeyes (No. 9) packing after their attempt at a Cinderella story moment. While UConn has won the tournament six times — most recently in 2022 and 2023 — the Illini have never taken home the title. The other side of the Final Four men's bracket features the final two remaining No. 1 seeds. Michigan defeated Tennessee (No. 6) to secure its spot in the semifinals, while Arizona held its spot as the top seed by beating Purdue (No. 2). The Michigan Wolverines have only been named the national champions once in 1989, while Arizona has also only won the tournament once in 1997. Who's in the women's Final Four? Serah Williams #22 and Sarah Strong #21 of the Connecticut Huskies on March 21, 2026 in Storrs, Connecticut; Agot Makeer #44 and Alicia Tournebize #31 of the South Carolina Gamecocks on March 30, 2026 in Sacramento, California. Joe Buglewicz/Getty; Harry How/Getty Unlike the men's tournament, the four remaining teams in the women's semifinals are all No. 1 seeds. While all of the teams are equally ranked, one of the Final Four games will be a rematch of the 2025 and 2022 National Championships. Last year, the UConn Huskies defeated the South Carolina Gamecocks to take home the national title, but the Gamecocks came out on top in 2022. This year, the teams will face off again in hopes of securing their position in the National Championship. Although UConn won in 2025, South Carolina won the year prior in 2024 against the University of Iowa and has a total of three national titles. Meanwhile, the UConn women's Huskies have won the tournament a total of 12 times, making the team the leader in the league. In addition to the 2025 rematch, the fellow No. 1 seeds, Texas and UCLA, will face off on the other side of the bracket. The Longhorns made it to the Final Four after beating the Michigan Wolverines (No. 2), while the UCLA Bruins defeated the Duke Blue Devils (No. 3). Texas has won the tournament once before in 1986, but UCLA has never taken home the title. The teams previously played against each other earlier in the season, when the Longhorns defeated the Bruins by 11 points in November. When are the men's Final Four and National Championship games? Yaxel Lendeborg #23 of the Michigan Wolverines on March 29, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois; Brayden Burries #5 of the Arizona Wildcats on March 28, 2026 in San Jose, California. Jamie Schwaberow/NCAA Photos via Getty; Bob Drebin/NCAA Photos via Getty The first men's Final Four game, which features UConn against Illinois, will take place on Saturday, April 4, at 6:09 p.m. ET at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Ind. The second game, Arizona vs. Michigan, follows the first game at approximately 8:49 p.m. ET at the same location. The winners of each game will face off in the 2026 National Championship on Monday, April 6, at 8:30 p.m. ET. When are the women's Final Four and National Championship games? Rori Harmon #3 of the Texas Longhorns on March 30, 2026 in Fort Worth, Texas; Lauren Betts #51 of the UCLA Bruins on March 29, 2026 in Sacramento, California. Elsa/Getty; Harry How/Getty The women's schedule is one day ahead of the men's tournament, so both Final Four games are scheduled for the evening of Friday, April 3. The UConn and South Carolina game tips off first at 7 p.m. ET at the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, with the UCLA and Texas game following at approximately 9:30 p.m. ET. The final two teams will compete in the 2026 National Championship game on Sunday, April 5, at 3:30 p.m. ET. Where can I watch and stream the men's Final Four and National Championship games? Brayden Burries #5 and Motiejus Krivas #13 of the Arizona Wildcats celebrate after the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament on March 28, 2026 in San Jose, California. Thearon W. Henderson/Getty The men's Final Four games and National Championship game will be simulcast on TBS, TNT and truTV. For people who don't have access to cable subscriptions, the games will also be available to stream on the NCAA March Madness Live App and HBO Max (with a standard or premium plan). All pregame and postgame coverage will also air simultaneously on TBS, TNT and truTV, and streaming on NCAA March Madness Live and HBO Max. Where can I watch and stream the women's Final Four and National Championship games? Sarah Strong #21 and Azzi Fudd #35 of the Connecticut Huskies speak during a press conference on April 02, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. Sarah Stier/Getty Unlike the men's tournament, the women's Final Four games and the National Championship game will be broadcast on different networks. Both Final Four games will be televised on ESPN, with a simultaneous alt-cast on ESPN2. Fans can also watch the semifinals in the ESPN App with a premium ESPN+ account or a compatible TV provider. However, the National Championship game on Sunday afternoon will primarily air on ABC, with an alt-cast on ESPN. Pregame coverage and postgame shows are also on both ABC and ESPN. The ESPN App and ESPN+ will also stream the final game. 0 seconds of 46 secondsVolume 0% 3 Things to Know About Alex Cooper
